subject: Action plan: telemetry request for intermittent streaming disconnects
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 15 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan: telemetry request for intermittent streaming disconnects

Team —

Quick context: SaaSlytics (large PLG analytics startup, prod traffic) reported intermittent streaming disconnects during long chat sessions (30–90s mark). They see partial outputs then a hard stop; no 500s on their side. This is blocking their pilot and we need a short-term mitigation + telemetry capture to root-cause.

What we have from the field (Marissa forwarded):
- session samples attached (saaslytics-session-samples.txt) with request IDs and timestamps
- disconnects are non-deterministic but cluster around 30–90s of active streaming
- customer running our hosted API via SDK v1.8.2 (Node)

Asks
1) Dev: what minimal runtime telemetry and traces do you need to triage (trace IDs, socket-level events, kernel metrics)?
2) Karthik: can the runtime toggle a keepalive/heartbeat or adjust streaming window for SaaSlytics as an immediate mitigation?
3) Marissa: can you get the exact SDK config and sample session ids from Alice (attached partially)?

Proposed immediate plan (short, 48–72h):
- Enable extended streaming telemetry for this customer (low-cost traces + sampling)
- Push a temporary SDK flag suggestion to customer to enable keepalive at 15s and retry-on-abort = true
- Patch runtime fallback to record last-kv-cache state at disconnect time (if feasible)

Please reply with what you need from the field and I'll coordinate with Alice for a secure upload of debug artifacts.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action plan: telemetry request for intermittent streaming disconnects

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Initial notes from runtime side: we have seen similar symptoms once when our connection pool evicts idle streams that have not registered heartbeats for ~60s under memory pressure. That eviction path currently logs at DEBUG only.

Immediate telemetry we need from customer:
- request IDs (we need the X-Request-ID in their headers) — samples attached look good but please confirm header name used by their SDK
- timestamps in UTC ISO for start/end of stream (we need millisecond precision)
- any intermediary network hops (CDN, proxy) visible to them

Runtime capabilities / quick mitigation options:
- We can flip a runtime flag to lower the eviction aggressiveness for their tenancy to 120s (safe short-term) — requires a dedicated rollout window but doable within 24h if approved
- We recommend SDK keepalive at 15s; in Node SDK that is currently an opt-in option (keepalive.pingInterval). If Marissa can push that change, it often reduces this class of disconnects
- As a diagnostic, enable socket-level logging for the affected process group; we can ingest that into a temporary bucket for 7 days

Longer-term items (needs PM sign-off):
- Expose a per-tenant eviction policy in the Console + a runtime metric lane for stream evictions
- Add an automatic sample-on-disconnect feature to capture KV cache and last 512 tokens at disconnect time (privacy review needed)

For immediate work, I'll stand up a short job to capture additional debug logs if Jordan confirms they can upload the session samples to the secure bucket. I attached a quick diagnostic-checklist.pdf with the exact trace names we need.

- Dev

--
Dev Patel
Principal Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Feb 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: streaming aborts — details from SaaSlytics

Forwarding customer's note (redacted):

From: Alice Turner <alice@saaslytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Feb 2028 07:50:12 -0800
Subject: Re: streaming aborts — examples attached

Hi Marissa,

Attaching two session samples (IDs: sess-9f3a, sess-9f4b). We see the server stop sending tokens mid-response. No 5xx on our side. We're on SDK v1.8.2; using default config. We proxy through an internal gateway and CloudFront in front.

Example snippet (sess-9f3a):
- start: 2028-02-15T16:01:22.123Z
- last token received: 2028-02-15T16:01:52.884Z
- aborted: connection closed without response body

We've enabled verbose client logs and attached them (saaslytics-session-samples.txt). Let us know what you need — Alice.

Marissa here — small ask: can we get the runtime to temporarily disable eviction for their tenancy and we'll push keepalive? Also, is it safe to send the session files into the secure bucket now?

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action plan: telemetry request for intermittent streaming disconnects

Thanks everyone — clear plan below and owners: 

1) Jordan: coordinate secure upload of saaslytics-session-samples.txt to the diagnostics bucket (I approve 7-day retention). Owner: Jordan. ETA: 2h.
2) Marissa: ask SaaSlytics to toggle keepalive.pingInterval = 15000ms in their SDK and restart one replica for verification. Owner: Marissa. ETA: 4 hours.
3) Dev: enable socket-level logging for the affected runtime shard and lower eviction aggressiveness for SaaSlytics tenancy to 120s. Owner: Dev. ETA: 24 hours for a controlled rollout.
4) Karthik: I'll create a Console feature request for per-tenant eviction policy and wire it into the roadmap for Q2. I'll also add a short eng spike to estimate automatic sample-on-disconnect. Owner: Karthik. ETA: feature spec by 2028-03-02.

If these actions reproduce or remove the disconnects, we'll use that to validate whether it's eviction-related vs SDK/proxy-level timeouts. We'll keep the customer updated and follow up with a short postmortem once we have root cause.

Please mark when actions complete.

Karthik
VP, Platform & Runtime
Redwood Inference
